name: deposition
what: 沉积: material carried in from outside and left in the cracks or on the surface (soil, iron). A physical process with physical parameters; 'old' is one of its results, not a knob (docs/layers.md). Fresh from the kiln: all zero. The crack network and the crack's own optics (the air film) are crafts/crackle.

tags.M: measured in a source, or by us on the photo/a render
tags.I: a value given by a source that did not measure it
tags.F: fitted on the material card against the photo (what was fitted, how)

crack_deposit.what: iron corrosion products (lepidocrocite + hematite) with quartz and clay deposited in the cracks during burial: Wu et al. 2025 (J. Beijing Univ. Chem. Technol. 52(5):133-144, Laohudong Guan sherds): golden thread is in the micro-cracks, light yellow-brown, poorly continuous, mostly deep in the crack and seen through the glaze as golden veins; in cross-section its colour fades with depth; the glaze itself has 0.52-1.10% Fe2O3, the iron comes from the burial environment and from the glaze's corrosion [M, Wu 2025]. Iron wire (biochar + pyrite) formed in firing [M, Wu 2025]: not on this sherd's photo, not modelled.

profile.value: the crack channel (crafts/crackle/faces.channels) is filled from top_mm below the mouth down to a depth drawn per column along the crack, so that the chance of being filled at depth z is c(z) = c0 erfc(z / L) (diffusion down the crack from the mouth with a constant source, L = 2 sqrt(D t)); the fill is opaque and diffuse (clay and silt grains), under and above it the crack stays an open air film
profile.tag: D: Wu 2025 sees the golden thread fade with depth [I]; the erfc of 1-D diffusion from a constant source is our reading of it [A]

spectrum.model: intimate mixture (Hapke 1981, J. Geophys. Res. 86:3039, isotropic scatterers): each endmember's reflectance r -> single-scattering albedo w = 1 - ((1 - r)/(1 + r))^2, w mixed linearly by the iron oxide's share f (lepidocrocite 'iron_oxide' or 'goethite', the state's 'mineral'), back with r = (1 - g)/(1 + g), g = sqrt(1 - w)
spectrum.tag: D (the model); the endmembers are measured spectra or an assumed white

iron_oxide.source: USGS Spectral Library v7 (Kokaly et al. 2017, DOI 10.3133/ds1035), Lepidocrocite GDS80 (synthetic; XRD: lepidocrocite and goethite in subequal parts, so not a pure phase), Beckman; fetched from a GitHub mirror of the library (stains research, S3), not checked against the USGS host

matrix_white.source: quartz and clay of the deposit (Wu 2025 names quartz and a clay-like matrix); a flat placeholder, no measured spectrum of the matrix
matrix_white.note: the default; a state can set its own flat matrix reflectance ('matrix', materials/guan_glaze/states.json), fitted [F]

goethite.source: USGS Spectral Library v7 (Kokaly et al. 2017, DOI 10.3133/ds1035), Goethite GDS134 (powder), 350-800 nm resampled to 10 nm; fetched from a GitHub mirror of the library (stains research, S3), not checked against the USGS host. The yellow iron oxyhydroxide of soils; Wu 2025 names lepidocrocite and hematite for Laohudong's golden thread, the Met sherd's own phase is not known [A: the choice]

top_mm.tag: A (card: the mouth emptied, e.g. by washing; F on the line test)

fill_corr_mm.tag: A: how fast the fill depth changes along the crack (beaded, discontinuous lines: Wu 2025's golden thread is 'poorly continuous' [I])

surface_stain.what: burial soil and iron on the glaze surface, blotches (materials/guan_glaze/glaze.stain_levels, card.py --stain-fraction); masked out of the card's comparison

states.moved: materials/guan_glaze/states.json: the parameter sets of the Guan card (fresh, heirloom, excavated) with the crack-wall corrosion and the surface roughness, which are not deposition
